answer: A grant for agents surveying a relic on the tundra coast beside the ocean allows one claim per human principal. Simultaneous in-person enrollment ceremonies issue one signed credential per live attendee. Claims prove that a campaign-specific nullifier derives from the credential; every alias of that credential yields the same value, and a ledger rejects repeats. To collect n grants, an operator must recruit n live attendees. This relies on honest issuers checking physical presence and preventing duplicate issuance; colluding humans remain a risk.
